title: Drop rare words: who gets their chance?
hook: A sampler throws away unlikely next words. What happens to the odds of the rest?

knows: that a language model gives each possible next word a chance
doesNotKnow: that a sampler can cut off the unlikely tail entirely
that the kept words are rescaled to share the removed chance

misconception: Sampling always includes every word, however unlikely, and cutting words leaves the others' chances unchanged.
objective: The learner can apply top-p: keep the fewest top words whose chances reach p, rescale them to total 100%, and say that cut words can no longer be drawn.

claims.text: The next-word odds after 'I ate' (pizza 45%, rice 30%, soup 15%, cake 6%, glue 4%) are invented, labelled 'Invented odds' on the stage.
claims.source: Brief 41 in company/domains/briefs/ai.md (odds 45/30/15/6/4); words added for readability. WORDS in Demo.tsx.

claims.text: At p = 85%, the top three words add to 45 + 30 + 15 = 90% (the top two give only 75%), so three are kept and cake and glue are cut; pizza's rescaled chance is 45/90 = 50%.
claims.source: keptCount(85) = 3, keptSum(3) = 90, share(0, 3) = 50 in Demo.tsx; node re-run: kept 3, sum 90, top 0.5. Start p = 75 keeps 2 (pizza 60%).

claims.text: Words cut by top-p cannot be drawn: in any set of 20 draws they come up 0 times.
claims.source: draw20(k, seed) in Demo.tsx samples only among the first k words (index never exceeds k - 1). Draw sets use mulberry32(seed = draw number 1, 2, ...), untuned; the zero count holds for every seed by construction.

claims.text: Top-p sampling, also called nucleus sampling, is used in some real text generators: it keeps the smallest set of top words whose probabilities reach p and renormalises them.
claims.source: About real systems: Holtzman, Buys, Du, Forbes & Choi 2020, 'The Curious Case of Neural Text Degeneration', ICLR (defines nucleus / top-p sampling as the smallest set with cumulative probability >= p, rescaled). 'Some real text generators' rather than 'all'.

recall.question: A sampler keeps only the top words whose chances add to at least 80%. Odds: 50%, 30%, 20%. What is the top word's chance after rescaling?
options: 50%: cutting words changes nothing for the others
62.5%: the two kept words (80%) are rescaled to 100%
recall.why: 50 + 30 = 80 reaches 80%, so two words stay; rescaling divides by 80, giving 50/80 = 62.5%. The 20% word can no longer be drawn.
